name: RFM95W
full_name: HopeRF RFM95W LoRa / FSK Sub-GHz Transceiver Module (SX1276-based)
description: Sub-GHz long-range transceiver module built around the Semtech SX1276, controlled over SPI. It supports both LoRa spread-spectrum and (G)FSK/OOK modulation, giving long range at low data rates with high link budget. The RFM95W covers the high sub-GHz bands (around 868 MHz EU / 915 MHz US/AU); sibling RFM96/98 cover lower bands. It runs from 1.8 to 3.7 V (3.3 V typical) with NON-5 V-tolerant logic, and exposes several configurable DIO pins for interrupts such as RxDone/TxDone.

pins.name: DIO0
pins.description: configurable digital I/O; commonly RxDone/TxDone interrupt

typical_application: Long-range, low-data-rate links: LoRaWAN nodes, remote telemetry/sensors over km distances, and point-to-point sub-GHz links.
gotchas: logic is NOT 5 V tolerant; a 5 V MCU needs level shifting on all SPI/DIO lines or the module is damaged
you must connect a correct antenna (or 50 ohm load) to ANT before transmitting; transmitting unloaded can destroy the PA
RFM95 covers the high band (868/915 MHz); RFM96/97/98 cover the low band - they are NOT interchangeable across bands despite identical footprint
DIO0 must be wired to an MCU interrupt for efficient RxDone/TxDone handling; polling works but wastes time
use the band/region legally allowed where you operate (e.g. 868 MHz EU, 915 MHz US); transmitting on the wrong band is illegal
the PA_BOOST vs RFO output path must match how the module is wired; selecting the wrong PA pin in software gives very low or no output
